name: 4-MTA
summary: Empathogen with very low chronic toxicity but high risk of acute harm due to mixed serotonin release and MAOI action. There are some reports that indicate it does not have a notable euphoric effect.

pharmacology.text: 4-MTA is a monoamine releasing agent (MRA). It was originally characterized as a selective serotonin releasing agent (SRA). However, the drug was subsequently found to more weakly induce the release of dopamine as well. 4-MTA shows a similar balance of monoamine reuptake inhibition as MDMA.
pharmacology.kind: Serotonin releasing agent; Monoamine oxidase inhibitor

uses.text: 4-Methylthioamphetamine (4-MTA), also known as para-methylthioamphetamine (MTA), is a serotonergic designer drug of the amphetamine family developed in the 1990s by a team led by David E. Nichols, an American pharmacologist and medical chemist, at Purdue University.
